Classic Chicken Soup for Breaking the Fast

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Serves 8-10Prep 25 minCook 2 hours 30 min

Chicken soup, often referred to as 'Jewish penicillin,' is a universally comforting and nourishing dish. For Yom Kippur, it holds special significance as the traditional meal to break the 25-hour fast, providing gentle sustenance and warmth after a day of reflection and prayer.

Ingredients

  • 1 (3-4 pound / 1.4-1.8 kg) whole chicken, cut into pieces, or 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) chicken backs and wings
  • 1 large yellow onion, unpeeled and quartered
  • 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks
  • 3 celery stalks, cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks
  • 1 large parsnip, peeled and cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks (optional)
  • 1 small bunch fresh dill, tied with kitchen twine
  • 1 small bunch fresh parsley, tied with kitchen twine
  • 1 teaspoon whole black peppercorns
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1 tablespoon kosher salt, or to taste
  • 12 cups (2.8 liters) cold water

Method

  1. Rinse the chicken pieces thoroughly under cold water and place them in a large (8-quart / 7.6-liter) stockpot.
  2. Add the quartered onion, carrots, celery, parsnip (if using), dill, parsley, peppercorns, and bay leaves to the pot with the chicken.
  3. Pour in the cold water, ensuring the chicken and vegetables are fully submerged. Add the kosher salt.
  4. Place the pot over medium-high heat and bring it to a gentle boil. As it heats, skim off any foam or scum that rises to the surface with a ladle or spoon.
  5. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot partially, and let it simmer gently for at least 2 to 2.5 hours, or until the chicken is very tender and the broth is flavorful.
  6. Carefully remove the chicken pieces from the pot and set aside to cool. Once cool enough to handle, remove the meat from the bones, discarding skin and bones. Shred or chop the chicken meat into bite-sized pieces.
  7. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot or large bowl, discarding the cooked vegetables and herbs. For a clearer broth, you can line the sieve with cheesecloth.
  8. Taste the broth and adjust seasoning with more salt if needed.
  9. Serve the hot broth with the reserved shredded chicken. Matzo balls, noodles, or additional fresh dill can be added to individual servings.

Tips

  • For an even richer flavor, roast the chicken bones and vegetables (except herbs) for 30 minutes at 400°F (200°C) before adding them to the pot.
  • To make the soup ahead, prepare it through straining, then refrigerate the broth and chicken separately. Reheat gently before serving.
  • For a clearer broth, ensure the soup never comes to a rolling boil during simmering; maintain a very gentle simmer.
